knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.:question/problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle -2,-1,1\rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle -2,-2,-1\rangle$, and $\mathbf{c}=\langle -3,2,k\rangle$ are coplanar.

The first-row expansion of their scalar triple product is provided:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})&=(-2)\cdot ((-2)\cdot (k)-(-1)\cdot (2))\\&\quad -(-1)\cdot ((-2)\cdot (k)-(-1)\cdot (-3))\\&\quad +(1)\cdot ((-2)\cdot (2)-(-2)\cdot (-3))
\end{aligned}
$$

Select the value of $k$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.:question/problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,-2,k\rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle -3,2,-1\rangle$, and $\mathbf{c}=\langle -3,1,k\rangle$ are coplanar.

The first-row expansion of their scalar triple product is provided:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})&=(1)\cdot ((2)\cdot (k)-(-1)\cdot (1))\\&\quad -(-2)\cdot ((-3)\cdot (k)-(-1)\cdot (-3))\\&\quad +(k)\cdot ((-3)\cdot (1)-(2)\cdot (-3))
\end{aligned}
$$

Select the value of $k$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.:question/problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle -1,3,2\rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle -2,k,2\rangle$, and $\mathbf{c}=\langle 3,2,-2\rangle$ are coplanar.

The first-row expansion of their scalar triple product is provided:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})&=(-1)\cdot ((k)\cdot (-2)-(2)\cdot (2))\\&\quad -(3)\cdot ((-2)\cdot (-2)-(2)\cdot (3))\\&\quad +(2)\cdot ((-2)\cdot (2)-(k)\cdot (3))
\end{aligned}
$$

Select the value of $k$.
